_doc: Hand-written narrative and run results of the fifth photo-match session (2026-11-16), read by write_test_status.py (counts in braces are filled from the data files) and printed by make_doc.py into REPORT.md. Nothing here is a result that was not seen; what was queued and not run says so.
title: ws10 photo-match (Q16) report, fifth session 2026-11-16 (fourth session 2026-11-15, third pass 2026-11-14, second pass 2026-11-13, first pass 2026-11-11)
scope_read: Scope read: CLAUDE.md (the Law and the Battle Theatre rules); the task text of the web workstream (photo-match continued: fetch the catalogued photographs that could not be read before, read each catalogue record for a stated camera position, search the National Park Service reports and pages for documented camera positions, register every pose with its tier, re-run the renderer, view the sheets, give a candid verdict per photograph, say plainly what would be needed); the report, the registry, the poses, the verdicts, the ledgers and the test file of the earlier sessions. Nothing was committed, pushed or deployed.
result_paragraph: Gate Q16 is **not passing** and `passes` is set nowhere. There are still **0 documented camera positions** (a coordinate, a lens and a plate: decision DD-PM-01); none of the {n_statements} camera-position statements now read gives one. What this session found: (1) **no photograph remained unread**: every digitized record of the registry had been fetched and looked at in the earlier sessions (the ledgers list 447 files of the first catalogue, 57 of the wide search and 82 further resources, each with sha256 and size; every entry has its saved file on disk, 11 originals of the first run having been deleted by design with their working copies kept, and the test file re-checks sizes and hashes wherever the file is present); the only records without an image are the 5 that the Library has not digitized. (2) **All {n_records} Library records were read again** from the open JSON of each record (191 fetched, 0 failed, 0 changed since the first reading); 37 hold a sentence that names a place or direction of view; each is a statement or has a written reading of why it is not (the place of the subject, a later photograph, a portrait); 4 records got a statement they had lacked (the Emmitsburg Road caption of 2018670908, the Rose-woods wording of 2008680497 and 2018670757 as leads, the staged card 2004682792 as a lead). (3) **A new primary source**: the Library holds Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book of the War as images only, but the master scans of the letterpress pages of the ten Gettysburg plates (35 to 44) are legible to OCR; they were read by machine and by eye. Plate 35, 'Gettysburg, Pennsylvania' (the exposure of poses P27 and P28), says in Gardner's own words: 'This view is taken from Cemetery Ridge, where our artillery was massed' and 'on the left of the picture can be seen Seminary Ridge'. It is a second source for the place, it names a ridge and not a building, and it gives no spot, bearing, height or lens; nine of the ten pages say nothing about where the camera stood. Gardner's catalogue of September 1863 (Library copy, OCR) and the Library's essays 'Does the Camera Ever Lie?' were read too: 13 statements were added in all (now {n_statements}); the essays say their analysis rests on Frassanito, so their statements of place are leads. (4) The staged-photograph flag of the sharpshooter series, which rested on the plan and on an unread National Archives blog, now also carries readable official words (NPS Then-And-Now: 'nor is it likely that the soldier fell in this location'; the body 'moved by the photographers from this location to another one some 40 yards away'; the Library essay: the photographers 'moved the corpse to this rocky niche and photographed him again'). (5) **The National Park Service texts were scanned again** with the same rule: 325 texts (the 118 of the earlier passes and 207 saved since, among them 51 HABS data pages, park newsletters and 12 hub pages fetched today), 359 passages, 19 in the new texts, none about the camera place of a July 1863 photograph. (6) **The renderer was re-run** for all 20 poses through the machine lock (120 files in 33 s): every file is byte-identical to the one the earlier sessions looked at, a second independent reproduction; compose.py rebuilt the 25 sheets, byte-identical to the earlier ones. (7) **All 20 pose sheets and the four lines images were opened and looked at again**; every verdict was read against its sheet; none changed: {matches} matches, {roughly} roughly, {dnot} does not, {cj} cannot judge over {n_poses} poses (P27 {v27}, P28 {v28}, P29 {v29}, P13 {v13}). No pose is called a match, and none can be: a fitted test is not a match and T-Q16-1 is unset. **What would settle Q16** (unchanged, and now narrower): station coordinates, lens and plate from the body that has them (the Gettysburg National Military Park: its museum or GIS staff for the Historic Photograph Collection prints GETT 41135 and the Then-And-Now stations; an owner act), the height and the 1863 form of the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse, an 1863 near-field model, landmark coordinates good to a few metres, and a value for T-Q16-1 written before the match.
what_was_run: State found: the earlier sessions' files intact (the test file 22 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped at the start; the render folders, ledgers and sheets present). The workflow text said that photographs 'could not be read before'; checking the ledgers against the disk showed that every one of the 447 ledger entries of the first catalogue (20 more are recorded as not offered: the medium file is kept; 11 originals were deleted by design and their working copies kept) and of the 57 of the wide search has its saved file, so nothing was left to fetch except what a record does not offer. Hosts tested on 2026-11-16: tile.loc.gov, www.loc.gov (open JSON), www.nps.gov, www.npshistory.com, catalog.archives.gov (a 5 KB application shell for every address, including api/v2 without a key) answered; museum.nps.gov, npgallery.nps.gov, irma.nps.gov, pubs.nps.gov and www.archives.gov were refused by the egress proxy (recorded as blocked, not worked around); the HTML pages of the Library essays answer 403 and were not retried (the open JSON of the same pages was read once each).

`render` through the lock: `PM_RENDER_DIR=tmp/photomatch/renders_rerun_20261116 tools/horde/bench.sh node tools/bt/photomatch/run.mjs` (all 20 poses, 120 PNG, queued at 02:34 UTC, rendered 02:48:09 to 02:48:42 UTC after about 14 minutes in the queue): every file is byte-identical to tmp/photomatch/renders (0 differing); `record_determinism.py --rerun-dir renders_rerun_20261116` wrote the second re-run into render_determinism.json beside the first (2026-11-15). Software GL only. One console line (a 404 for a resource of the render page) appears in every run and changes no pixel.

`compose.py` (20 s of CPU): the 25 sheets of tools/bt/photomatch/reports are byte-identical to the earlier ones. The 20 pose sheets (P01 to P29), the lines images of P27, P28 and P29 and the 50 degree lines image of P28 were opened and looked at with the Read tool; the verdicts were read against them; none changed.

`loc_reread.py` (191 requests at one per 1.2 s, polite, no retry on a block): the open JSON of every registered record, saved under tmp/library/web/photomatch/fourth/loc_items with sha256; compared with the copy of the first reading: 0 changed; `loc_reread_review.py`: the 15 records whose own words name a place or direction of view and that no statement covers were read, one line each (the place of the subject, a later photograph, a portrait; loc_reread_review.json).

`fifth_texts.py`, `sketch_master_ocr.py`, `build_sketchbook_concordance.py`: the Library's digitized copy of Gardner's Sketch Book (ppmsca.12834): 112 album pages per volume, order letterpress page then plate; the 1024-px derivative gave unusable OCR; the master scans (100 MB each) of album pages 77, 79, 81, 83, 85, 87, 89, 91, 93 and 95 were fetched one at a time (size equal to Content-Length), read with tesseract 5.3.4 and deleted (sha256 of every scan and text in sketchbook_v1/manifest.json); the printed titles and credits of the ten plates were read by eye. Plate 35 states the place; the others do not. The Library's own call numbers tie the plates to records 2006685383 to 2006692515.

`build_statements.py`: 13 statements added (3 from the Sketch Book letterpress, 3 from Gardner's catalogue of September 1863, 4 from Library records, 3 from the Library essays), every quote found in its saved text (the three fragments of the plate 35 sentence in order); 78 sources; evidence lines R12.032 to R12.035 rebuilt. `add_verdicts_fifth_pass.py`: a paragraph for P27 and P28 (the frame positions of Seminary Ridge and the Seminary building computed from the gazetteer and the footprint with the bearing formula of run.mjs), the gate block (statement count read from the file, the new sources named, the date of the review). `build_registry.py`: the registry rebuilt (191 records; 18 posed, 173 cannot judge); the staged basis of 19 flagged records carries the readable official sources; the plate records carry the Sketch Book sentence.

National Park Service: `scan_nps_photos.py` run again (325 texts, 359 passages); `nps_scan_review.py` read the 19 passages of the newly scanned texts (none about a July 1863 camera place). Twelve pages of the park's history and photo hubs that had not been saved were fetched with webget.py (1 request per 1.3 s; stories, people, places and preservation hubs were listed, the new ones saved); the hub listing names 30 further pages: those about July 1863 photographs (Then-And-Now, Devil's Den, Little Round Top, Rose Woods, Trostle, buildings and farms) were saved in the earlier sessions.

`webget.py` repaired: a transfer cut short by the network answered HTTP 200 with 53 KB of a 250 KB JSON (manifest lines 101 and 102 of the same URL); the fetcher now treats a nonzero exit of curl as a failure and retries twice (decision DD-PM-16); the 107 saved NPS HTML pages were checked: all end with the closing html tag.

`update_library_3.py` run (the pointer files acquired_3.json and status_3.json): 4 items added (Sketch Book letterpress, Gardner's catalogue, the Library essays, the fresh reading of the records), the Sketch Book entry moved from 'images only' to found, two blocked entries added (the refused NPS and National Archives hosts); a defect found in the script (it stamped today's date on the fetch date of items it merely re-wrote) was fixed so that a re-run never rewrites a fetch date.

Documents rebuilt from the data (`make_doc.py`): PHOTOMATCH.md (a new section on the photographer's own words; both the copy audit tests pass); this report. Proposed register entries ws10-EG-01, 05, 06 and 14 received an update row of 2026-11-16. Delegated decisions DD-PM-13 to DD-PM-17 were appended to decisions/DELEGATED-DECISIONS-2026-11-11.md.
findings: Gardner's letterpress for plate 35 gives three readings for the heading of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge exposure that no single heading meets at an assumed 40 degree field: north (the Cemetery Landscape Report), northwest (the Record of Treatment) and Seminary Ridge on the left of the picture (Gardner). At the north word the Seminary and the ridge lie outside the frame; at the northwest word the ridge stands at 0.18 and the Seminary at 0.47 of the frame width but the pike falls at the right edge and the court house is outside the frame; the tower-implied heading (337 to 343 degrees, a fit and not a test) lies between. All three are carried, none chosen (EG-14, DD-PM-15).

The Sketch Book (1866) credits plate 35 to T. H. O'Sullivan; Gardner's catalogue of September 1863 lists no. 273 'Gettysburg from the Cemetery' (the negative number the NPS cites, LC-B815-273) in a block of negatives that the ditto marks of its OCR text assign to Jas. F. Gibson. Attribution does not bear on the camera place and is carried, not resolved.

The Library essay on plates 36 and 37 (analysis attributed to Frassanito) puts the two views in open fields near the Rose farm and close to the Emmitsburg Road, while the Library's own caption of the negative of plate 37 says near the McPherson woods; carried as a conflict of place, both as they stand, with the essay's statement a lead.

The earlier sessions' registry text for record 2018670908 said that no place is stated beyond the Rose-woods area; its negative sleeve caption, which repeats Gardner's own title no. 268 of 1863, says 'near the Emmitsburg Road'; the text was corrected.

A transfer that reported HTTP 200 but was cut short had been accepted by the fetcher (53 KB of 250 KB); no saved NPS HTML page was affected (all end with the closing tag), and the PDFs and images were verified by size and hash in the earlier sessions; the fetcher is repaired.

The park museum catalogue (the Historic Photograph Collection, GETT 41135) lives on hosts that the egress proxy refuses (museum.nps.gov, npgallery.nps.gov); it is the most likely place for station coordinates, and only the park can open it (owner step).
tests: `node --test docs/battle-theatre/app/tests/photomatch-q16.test.mjs` (run directly: no browser): {q16_pass} pass, {q16_fail} fail, {q16_skip} skipped (the optional render test) of {q16_tests} tests. Seven tests were added: the fresh reading of every record and the written reading of each cue; the Sketch Book concordance (plates, call numbers, hashes, the quotes of plate 35 in order in the saved machine reading); Gardner's catalogue and the essays as sources (the essays are leads); the staged flags with the readable official words (each quote asserted in its saved text); the NPS rescan review and the repaired fetcher; the determinism record with both re-runs and the fifth gate block. No threshold was lowered and no test loosened; the pre-written criteria and the thresholds of tie_geometry.py are asserted unchanged.

`node --test tests/photomatch.test.mjs` (the old test in the repository's tests/ folder, outside this task's ownership): not run again; it fails 3 of 5 on the new ledger and schema as in the earlier sessions (request notes bt-web-photomatch-old-test.md and bt-gates-photomatch-test-host-rule.md); it is not part of the app suite.
owed: No real-GPU rendering: every render is software GL (SwiftShader); nothing here is a timing or a real-GPU visual result.

The park's own records: station coordinates, lens and plate of the Then-And-Now pictures and of the prints that the Record of Treatment cites by number (GETT 41135); the museum hosts are refused here. An owner act: ask the park.
The five records of the wide search that the Library has not digitized; the National Archives catalog (an application shell without a key: an owner act) and the NARA Prologue blog (refused host).

The photographs of the Sketch Book plates were not matched against the catalogued images by features this session (the Library's call numbers tie them to their records, and plates 35 to 44 are already among the catalogued exposures); the printed titles and credits were read by eye from the 1024-px page images, not by machine.
Master scans of the photographs themselves were not fetched except the two of the first session; matching at full resolution is not needed to say that no camera position is documented.
The skyline test could not be applied to the other poses: they have no documented place, and the NPS area words (a farm, a hill) do not fix the camera within the depth of the scene.
